data.productDescription: Height of the top of canopy above bare earth (Canopy Height Model (CHM)). Data are mosaicked over the AOP footprint; mosaicked onto a spatially uniform grid at 1 m spatial resolution, and delivered as 1 km by 1 km tiles. Data are provided in GeoTIFF (.tif) format. Associated metadata files include QA reports (.pdf, .md, .html), shapefile boundaries (.shp, .shx, .prj, .dbf), and .kml boundary files; shapefile and kml boundary files may be zipped (.zip).
data.productAbstract:
Forests store and sequester a considerable proportion of the terrestrial global carbon budget. Forest canopy metrics are directly measurable with LiDAR sensors because laser pulses will be reflected from the uppermost canopy layers and remaining energy will penetrate to, and reflect from, under-story and the ground surface. The near simultaneous direct measurement of ground and canopy elevation allows the canopy height to be estimated through differencing. The CHM is generated by creating a continuous surface of canopy height estimates across the entire spatial domain of the LiDAR survey. The CHM is derived directly from the LiDAR point cloud. To produce the CHM, the point cloud is separated into classes representing the ground and vegetation returns. The ground classified points allow calculation of a height normalized point cloud to provide a relative estimate of vegetation elevation. A surface is then generated using the height normalized vegetation points to produce the CHM. For data collected with the Optech Gemini sensor (operated between 2012-2020), any canopy heights less than 2m are set to zero. NEON has been updating it's lidar sensors over the years, and data product quality has improved as technology has improved. For data collected with the Optech Galaxy Prime (2018+), Riegl Q780 (2021+), or Riegl VQ-780 II-S (2025+) sensors, any canopy heights less than 0.7 m are set to zero.  Please refer to https://www.neonscience.org/data-collection/lidar for more details about NEON's lidar sensors and the derived data products.

Latency:
AOP data are expected to be available 60 days after the final collection day at a site.
data.productDesignDescription: The Ecosystem Structure product is a canopy height model (CHM) in GeoTIFF raster data format in UTM projection and ITRF00 datum. The CHM is normalized by ground height, indicating all ground elevations are set to zero and canopy height is the height of vegetation above the ground in meters. A pit-free algorithm is used following Khosravipour et al. 2013 & 2014 (see the Algorithm Theoretical Basis Document for more details). The CHM rasters for a site are distributed in 1 km by 1 km tiles. The coordinate of the lower left (south-west) corner of the tile are provided in the filename.
data.productStudyDescription: NEON AOP data are planned for yearly collects at all NEON sites at 90% of maximum greenness or greater. Coverage is planned to include at least 95% of NIS Tower Airshed area as well as at least 80% of a minimum 10 km x 10 km box around that for terrestrial sites. All acquisitions are subject to change due to weather conditions as well as program planning changes.
data.productBasicDescription: Includes the data product as a 1 km by 1 km mosaic tile in a single band orthorectified GeoTIFF (.tif).
data.productExpandedDescription: An expanded package is not available for this product.
data.productRemarks: In 2024, the Ecosystem Structure / CHM data product was added to the Google Earth Engine (GEE) [Publisher Data Catalogs](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/publisher/neon-prod-earthengine) as an Image Collection. Details about this GEE dataset can be found here: https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/projects_neon-prod-earthengine_assets_CHM_001. CHM data available on GEE may not represent the full archive of data available on the NEON Data Portal. Additional site visits can be added to GEE upon request by emailing listaopgee@battelleecology.org.

changeLogs.issue: Original algorithm did not take advantage of improvements in the Riegl Lidar to handle short stature vegetation. CHM heights < 2 m were set to zero, instead of heights < 2/3 m.
changeLogs.resolution: Algorithm was updated to improve data product quality for short stature vegetation when the Riegl lidar was used for data collection.

changeLogs.issue: Files referenced in incorrect UTM zone (16N) for the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest region of STEI.
changeLogs.resolution: Files were reprocessed and referenced within the correct UTM zone (15N).

changeLogs.issue: Data was incorrectly referenced to UTM Zone 33N instead of Zone 13N
changeLogs.resolution: Data was reprocessed as part of RELEASE-2024 CHM reprocessing effort, and UTM zone reference was correctly set to 13N.

changeLogs.issue: Some 'No Data' values at site edges coded as NaNs instead of -9999.

The algorithm for determining the canopy height model (CHM) introduced artifacts which could be identified by viewing a histogram of canopy heights across the entire survey. Artifacts manifested as sharp reductions in canopy height at 5 m intervals.
changeLogs.resolution: Applied an updated implementation of the CHM algorithm which removed artifacts. See https://www.neonscience.org/impact/observatory-blog/aop-data-availability-notification-release-2024 for more details.

changeLogs.issue: AOP discrete lidar point cloud data were found to have abnormally high noise levels, which the standard noise filtering algorithms did not correctly classify. This mis-classification passed through to higher-level data products.  In most cases, a small portion of each site is affected by this issue, and the large majority of the site is still accurately classified.
changeLogs.resolution: Regions with dense and high levels of atmospheric noise were manually removed and downstream products were re-generated. 2018 CLBJ, 2019 and 2021 MOAB and 2022 TOOL were fixed for RELEASE-2025. 2019 PUUM, REDB, and UKFS, and UNDE were uploaded provisionally and will be included in RELEASE-2026.

changeLogs.issue: Mis-alignment in the discrete lidar line to line adjustments. Some portions of the flight box were found to have tens of centimeters to up to meters of vertical differences between flight lines, which affected all downstream lidar products.
changeLogs.resolution: 2014 DSNY & HARV, 2018 ABBY: Lidar lines were properly aligned using BayesMap StripAlign software and made available in RELEASE-2025. For the remainder of the sites and dates, lidar data will be reprocessed and made available as part of RELEASE-2026.
